scenarios.title: Customer Support Resolution Agent
scenarios.narrative: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom MCP tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.
keyProps: MCP tools: get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human
High-ambiguity requests: returns, billing disputes, account issues

scenarios.title: Code Generation with Claude Code
scenarios.narrative: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.
keyProps: Custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration
Plan mode vs direct execution decisions

scenarios.title: Multi-Agent Research System
scenarios.narrative: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.
keyProps: Coordinator plus four subagents: web search, document analysis, synthesis, report generation
Cited reports require provenance to survive synthesis
Failures must propagate with enough context for coordinator recovery

scenarios.title: Developer Productivity with Claude
scenarios.narrative: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with MCP servers.
keyProps: Built-in tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
Large unfamiliar codebases and long exploration sessions
MCP servers extend the built-in toolset

scenarios.title: Claude Code for Continuous Integration
scenarios.narrative: You are integrating Claude Code into your CI/CD pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.
keyProps: Blocking pre-merge checks vs overnight analysis

scenarios.title: Structured Data Extraction
scenarios.narrative: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JSON schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.
keyProps: tool_use with JSON schemas for guaranteed structure
Validation-retry loops and semantic vs syntax errors
Batch processing and human review routing

prepPlan.title: Build an agent with the Claude Agent SDK
prepPlan.detail: Implement a complete agentic loop with tool calling, error handling, and session management. Practice spawning subagents and passing context between them.

prepPlan.title: Configure Claude Code for a real project
prepPlan.detail: Set up CLAUDE.md with a configuration hierarchy, create path-specific rules in .claude/rules/, build custom skills with frontmatter options (context: fork, allowed-tools), and integrate at least one MCP server.

prepPlan.title: Design and test MCP tools
prepPlan.detail: Write tool descriptions that clearly differentiate similar tools. Implement structured error responses with error categories and retryable flags. Test tool selection reliability with ambiguous requests.

prepPlan.title: Build a structured data extraction pipeline
prepPlan.detail: Use tool_use with JSON schemas, implement validation-retry loops, design schemas with optional/nullable fields, and practice batch processing with the Message Batches API.

prepPlan.title: Practice prompt engineering techniques
prepPlan.detail: Write few-shot examples for ambiguous scenarios. Define explicit review criteria to reduce false positives. Design multi-pass review architectures for large code reviews.

prepPlan.title: Study context management patterns
prepPlan.detail: Practice extracting structured facts from verbose tool outputs, implementing scratchpad files for long sessions, and designing subagent delegation to manage context limits.

prepPlan.title: Review escalation and human-in-the-loop patterns
prepPlan.detail: Understand when to escalate (policy gaps, customer requests, inability to progress) versus resolve autonomously. Practice designing human review workflows with confidence-based routing.

exercises.title: Build a Multi-Tool Agent with Escalation Logic
exercises.objective: Practice designing an agentic loop with tool integration, structured error handling, and escalation patterns.
steps: Define 3-4 MCP tools with detailed descriptions that clearly differentiate each tool's purpose, expected inputs, and boundary conditions. Include at least two tools with similar functionality that require careful description to avoid selection confusion.
Implement an agentic loop that checks stop_reason to determine whether to continue tool execution or present the final response. Handle both "tool_use" and "end_turn" correctly.

Add structured error responses to your tools: errorCategory (transient/validation/permission), isRetryable boolean, and human-readable descriptions. Test that the agent retries transient errors and explains business errors to the user.
Implement a programmatic hook that intercepts tool calls to enforce a business rule (e.g. blocking operations above a threshold amount), redirecting to an escalation workflow when triggered.
Test with multi-concern messages and verify the agent decomposes the request, handles each concern, and synthesizes a unified response.

exercises.title: Configure Claude Code for a Team Development Workflow
exercises.objective: Practice configuring CLAUDE.md hierarchies, custom slash commands, path-specific rules, and MCP server integration for a multi-developer project.
steps: Create a project-level CLAUDE.md with universal coding standards and testing conventions. Verify instructions placed at project level are applied consistently across all team members.
Create .claude/rules/ files with YAML frontmatter glob patterns for different code areas (e.g. paths: ["src/api/**/*"], paths: ["**/*.test.*"]). Test that rules load only when editing matching files.
Create a project-scoped skill in .claude/skills/ with context: fork and allowed-tools restrictions. Verify the skill runs in isolation without polluting the main conversation context.
Configure an MCP server in .mcp.json with environment variable expansion for credentials. Add a personal experimental MCP server in ~/.claude.json and verify both are available simultaneously.
Test plan mode versus direct execution on a single-file bug fix, a multi-file library migration, and a new feature with multiple valid approaches. Observe when plan mode provides value.

exercises.title: Build a Structured Data Extraction Pipeline
exercises.objective: Practice designing JSON schemas, using tool_use for structured output, implementing validation-retry loops, and designing batch processing strategies.
steps: Define an extraction tool with a JSON schema containing required and optional fields, an enum with an "other" + detail string pattern, and nullable fields. Verify the model returns null rather than fabricating values when fields are absent.

Implement a validation-retry loop: on validation failure send a follow-up request including the document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation error. Track which errors are resolvable via retry (format mismatches) versus which are not (information absent from source).
Add few-shot examples demonstrating extraction from documents with varied formats (inline citations vs bibliographies, narrative vs tables) and verify improved handling of structural variety.

Design a batch processing strategy: submit 100 documents via the Message Batches API, handle failures by custom_id, resubmit failed documents with modifications (e.g. chunking oversized documents), and calculate total processing time relative to SLA constraints.
Implement a human review routing strategy: output field-level confidence scores, route low-confidence extractions to human review, and analyze accuracy by document type and field.

exercises.title: Design and Debug a Multi-Agent Research Pipeline
exercises.objective: Practice orchestrating subagents, managing context passing, implementing error propagation, and handling synthesis with provenance tracking.
steps: Build a coordinator that delegates to at least two subagents. Ensure the coordinator's allowedTools includes "Task" and that each subagent receives findings directly in its prompt rather than relying on automatic context inheritance.
Implement parallel subagent execution by emitting multiple Task tool calls in a single response. Measure the latency improvement compared to sequential execution.

Design structured subagent output separating content from metadata: each finding should include a claim, evidence excerpt, source URL/document name, and publication date. Verify synthesis preserves attribution.

Implement error propagation: simulate a subagent timeout and verify the coordinator receives structured error context (failure type, attempted query, partial results). Test that it can proceed with partial results and annotate coverage gaps.

Test with conflicting source data and verify the synthesis output preserves both values with source attribution rather than arbitrarily selecting one, distinguishing well-established from contested findings.

policies.title: Scoring
policies.body: Criterion-referenced: you are measured against a fixed standard, not a curve. Scaled score 100–1,000 with a cut score of 720, set by a formal standard-setting study of minimally qualified candidate performance. Domain percentages on the score report are informational only; pass/fail is based on the total scaled score.

policies.title: Registration and scheduling
policies.body: Register through the Anthropic Partner Academy (checkout reflects any partner-tier discount), then create a Pearson VUE account and schedule. Choose online proctoring or a Pearson test center. Cancel or reschedule up to 24 hours before the appointment; changes inside 24 hours forfeit the fee.

policies.title: Identification
policies.body: Valid, unexpired, government-issued photo ID whose name matches your registration exactly. Name corrections go to certifications-support@anthropic.com before scheduling.

policies.title: Retakes
policies.body: Waiting periods grow with each failure: 14 days after the first, 30 after the second, 90 after the third. Maximum four attempts per exam in a rolling twelve months. The fee applies to every attempt. Limits are per exam.

policies.title: Accommodations
policies.body: Requested and approved by Pearson VUE before scheduling, at pearsonvue.com/us/en/test-takers/accommodations. Do not schedule until approval arrives.

policies.title: Exam-day conduct
policies.body: Stay in view of the webcam if testing online. Workspace clear of notes, books, phones, secondary monitors. No communication with anyone. No capturing or reproducing exam content. Prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, headphones, study materials, recording devices.

policies.title: NDA
policies.body: You must accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement before the exam begins. Declining ends the session with no refund.

policies.title: Recertification
policies.body: Valid 12 months. Renew on time with a free, non-proctored assessment on the Anthropic Partner Academy after reviewing what changed. A lapsed credential requires retaking the full exam at full fee. Significant content changes may force a full retake instead of the renewal assessment.

policies.title: Appeals
policies.body: Within 14 days of notification, or of the exam date for a result concern, via Pearson VUE support. The standard-setting outcome and individual item content are not appealable.

strategy.title: The exam rewards proportionate responses
strategy.body: Across the twelve official sample questions the correct answer is almost always the smallest change that addresses the stated root cause. Distractors are systematically over-engineered: routing classifiers, trained models, sentiment analysis, speculative caching. Before picking, name the root cause in the stem, then find the option that hits it directly.

strategy.title: Determinism beats persuasion
strategy.body: When a business rule must hold every time (verify identity before refunding, block refunds over $500), the answer is programmatic: hooks, prerequisite gates. Prompt instructions and few-shot examples have a non-zero failure rate and are never the right answer for guaranteed compliance.

strategy.title: Read the logs in the stem
strategy.body: Several items hand you the diagnosis. If the coordinator's log shows a narrow decomposition, the coordinator is the fault, not the downstream agents that executed their assignments correctly.

strategy.title: Root cause, not symptom
strategy.body: Poor tool selection with minimal descriptions is a description problem, not a few-shot problem. Attention dilution across 14 files is a decomposition problem, not a context-window-size problem.

strategy.title: Know what is explicitly out of scope
strategy.body: Streaming, vision, computer use, prompt caching internals, rate limits, pricing math, OAuth and cloud provider configuration will not be tested. If an option leans on one of those, it is very likely a distractor.

strategy.title: Watch the response count
strategy.body: Items are multiple-choice or multiple-response and each states how many to select. Multiple-response items are usually all-or-nothing; count before you commit.

strategy.title: Budget the clock
strategy.body: 60 items in 120 minutes is 2 minutes each. Scenario narratives are reused across several items, so the first item in a scenario costs more reading time and later ones cost less. Flag and move on rather than stalling.
